analysis:
Examined the protocol-messages.md doc updates (units 9-11), the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump, and the EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift patch.

The Swift change makes performance-rate freshness follow the newest observation (`at = max(at, now)`, gated by `DeadlineAdmissionFixes.enabled`), so late-arriving completed samples cannot shorten reported sample age. It adds `coversObservation` and `observationAge` helpers. The wire shape is unchanged, per the doc. These are transient capacity and performance fields (deadline admission), diagnostic and observability evidence. They carry no prompt content, keys, attestation, authorization or billing data.

Possible effect: a malicious provider already controls its own self-reported performance telemetry. The change does not add a new trust grant. The coordinator validates freshness and does not accept the rates as certification, according to the docs for deadline_profile and deadline_work. The docs changed only the sample_age_ms description and added a producer note. No existing threat in the supplied model (A-001, T-007, T-041, TB-002, TB-007) is weakened by this.

Caveats: the submodule bump (libs/mlx-swift-lm from 0351444 to e28f89d) is opaque. Its contents are not supplied, so any security impact on the inference engine (TB-007), the prefix cache (T-041) or memory handling cannot be assessed. The patch excerpt for the Swift file is truncated, and callers of `observe`/`coversObservation` were not seen. I recommend a review of the submodule diff.
